question: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. B and C together can complete the same work in 15 days. C and A together can do it in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the job?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 12, 15 and 20 = 60 units.

Combined efficiencies: (A + B) = 60 ÷ 12 = 5, (B + C) = 60 ÷ 15 = 4, (C + A) = 60 ÷ 20 = 3.

Total efficiency of 2(A + B + C) = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 ⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 6.

Efficiency of A = Total Efficiency − Efficiency of (B + C) = 6 − 4 = 2 units/day.

Time taken by A alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of A = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 12 days

Time taken by B and C together = 15 days

Time taken by C and A together = 20 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Adding all the combined efficiencies: (A + B) + (B + C) + (C + A) = 5 + 4 + 3

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 12

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of A = (Efficiency of A + B + C) − (Efficiency of B + C)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 6 − 4 = 2 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept works exactly like Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling) and outlet pipes have negative efficiency (emptying).

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each person. If the working time is equal for all, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and use it to find the number of cycles required to complete the total work.
